result.architecture_summary: A local-supervisor-owned pipeline with immutable, Git-anchored evidence as the authority for "done" (not mutable task status or model self-report), a documented GER repair loop with mandatory runtime evidence, provider-neutral AgentRuntime contracts (AgentInvocationRequest/AgentResult) with fail-closed capability/budget enforcement, and a multi-role ArchitectureReview process used as a periodic self-check. As of the frozen commit, execution authority (readiness/dispatch/repository_write/approved_command_execution) is deliberately disabled everywhere; the only capabilities implemented for either provider (Claude, Codex) are read-only repository inspection used exclusively to run ArchitectureReview on itself. No gameplay code has been produced through the new AgentRuntime/TaskExecution path; the only shipped feature (NSC-023 fixed isometric camera) was built earlier via ad hoc Assignment 5/6 scripts, not the current production path.
result.verdict_reason: The core authority/state model is genuinely sound: mutable task metadata cannot authorize execution, evidence is bound to committed Git objects, provider claims are explicitly non-authoritative, runtime evidence is mandatory over static pass, and a no-op-refinement guard exists — all traceable to real observed failures (Assignment 6's camera, the 8/8 "partially_unsound" review). But two straight days of post-Milestone-1 work produced zero gameplay progress and, more importantly, built zero capability for the one thing an autonomous coding pipeline must eventually do: let a bounded worker write a file and have that write deterministically checked. repository_write and approved_command_execution remain unsupported in both providers after four provider-adapter stages (4A–4D); the only capability actually exercised is read-only inspection used to run the review tool on itself, twice. This is not a fundamentally wrong design, but effort has been allocated to hardening and self-review far ahead of proving the actual delivery loop, which is the definition of overbuilt relative to current evidence.
strong_decisions: Mutable task status cannot authorize execution; completion is derived from immutable Git-anchored evidence records (Phase 3A), independently re-derivable at any HEAD.

Provider results are explicitly non-authoritative claims (claimed_changed_paths, claimed_test_commands, claims_execution_occurred) that must be independently checked by deterministic Git/Unity/TaskGraph logic — a correct answer to 'self-evaluation risk.'
Runtime evidence is mandatory, not optional, for interactive Unity behavior (ADR-015), directly derived from the real camera-facing-wrong-direction failure in Assignment 6.
A no-op refinement is treated as a failed, budget-consuming repair attempt (ADR-016), closing a real observed false-success/infinite-loop path.
Dispatch/readiness/execution authorization are explicitly and verifiably disabled (`taskcontrol ready` / `authorize` fail closed) rather than merely undocumented, preventing premature autonomy.

write_boundaries.allowed_paths/denied_paths and per-request capability enforcement are modeled in the immutable contract layer before any provider implements writing, so scope containment doesn't have to be retrofitted later.
ADR-038's acceptance of a trusted single-user read boundary instead of building a hardened sandbox is a correct, evidence-proportionate YAGNI call.

The architecture-review process explicitly warns its own reviewers that shared model-family bias is not independent proof and forbids vote-counting in synthesis — an unusually self-aware treatment of correlated LLM failure for a review-of-itself mechanism.
structural_flaws: Canonical-GDD binding in current_conformance.py hashes the entire GDD file (canonical_text_sha256 over Docs/GDD/No_Safe_Circle_GDD.md) rather than the specific sections a task's gdd_evidence cites. Any GDD edit, anywhere, forces every task's existing evidence into needs_revalidation, including tasks the edit has nothing to do with. For a project whose GDD is explicitly expected to keep changing while the game is built, this guarantees compounding revalidation/human-approval overhead as the graph grows past its current single conformant task.

There is no middle tier between 'do nothing' and 'run the full multi-model Reconciliation Verification Crew' for handling a GDD change. Full reconciliation is explicitly reserved for bootstrap/major events, but no scoped/diff-based impact-analysis tool exists yet to answer 'which of the 37 tasks does this specific GDD edit actually affect.' CURRENT_STATE.md names this as future work, which means the moving-design-target problem this review is specifically asked to weigh is currently unsolved, not merely deferred with a stopgap.

The entire Stage 3/4 AgentRuntime effort has only ever exercised repository_read/repository_search capabilities through ArchitectureReview, a read-only, non-Unity, non-write meta-workload. repository_write and approved_command_execution — the capabilities an actual Implementer role requires — remain unimplemented in every provider, so the hardest and riskiest part of the architecture (safe scoped writes, Git worktree isolation, Unity invocation from a container) is completely unvalidated despite four stages of provider-adapter work.
observed_failure_solutions: ADR-015/runtime evidence requirement — from the camera facing the wrong direction after passing static evaluation.
ADR-016/no-op refinement guard — from the Refiner reporting 'implemented' while making no changes under Assets/.
Phase 1-3 evidence-derived conformance model — direct response to the 8/8-reviewer finding that mutable task status could assert false completion.
ADR-036 (build vs. adopt agent-mux/agent-shell) — from a real spike finding concrete incompatibilities (Linux build patch needed, weaker fail-closed behavior).
Migration-report Windows CRLF/BOM normalization — from real Git-for-Windows line-ending friction encountered during the schema-2.0 migration.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Extensive AgentRuntime contract hardening against Windows-reserved device names, path traversal, control characters, and drive-letter paths for a single trusted developer on a single machine (ADR-038 itself concedes this is a trusted single-user context).
The Codex turn-to-timeout mapping (30 seconds/turn) is an invented, admittedly 'temporary,' non-cross-provider-equivalent policy with no observed data behind the constant.
Provider-namespaced outputs/claude vs outputs/codex and a future 'Claude-versus-Codex comparison' scaffold, built before any comparison consumer exists.
The Reconciliation Verification Crew's heavy multi-model streaming-refinement/conflict-arbiter machinery is sized for a one-time bootstrap event explicitly marked 'must not be rerun.'

Running the full 8-reviewer + synthesis + adversarial-critique ArchitectureReview twice in two days (once per provider) to validate a provider-plumbing migration, rather than to evaluate a material architecture or product decision.
overengineering: Two independent hand-rolled 'atomic immutable JSON artifact' implementations (AgentRunner._publish using os.link no-clobber semantics; architecture_review.safe_write_json using tmp.replace overwrite semantics) exist for conceptually the same audit-artifact pattern in two adjacent layers, with different immutability guarantees, instead of one shared primitive.

Four completed provider-adapter stages (4A-4D) invested in capability mapping, budget translation, and Docker service separation before a single write-capable capability exists to justify the abstraction surface.

Provider-scoped output namespacing, resume-across-namespace refusal, and a dual-provider launcher concept are built out for future cross-provider comparison work that is explicitly 'future work' and has no current consumer.
missing_components: A write-capable provider path (repository_write) with Git worktree/branch isolation, so a worker can actually edit a file under a bounded, deterministically-checked scope.
A scoped GDD-change impact analyzer between 'do nothing' and 'full multi-model reconciliation' for the routine iterative-editing case this review was specifically asked to weigh.
Any ExecutionCrew/Implementer orchestration — TaskExecution today only wraps AgentRuntime with an audit record; it does not select, dispatch, branch, or merge work.

Any real throughput data: no gameplay ticket has ever gone through claim → context → implement → evaluate → merge on the production path, so 'materially faster development' remains an untested hypothesis, not a measured result.
state_and_authority_concerns: Whole-document GDD hashing as the sole conformance-invalidation trigger conflates 'the GDD changed' with 'this task's requirements changed,' duplicating authority between the canonical GDD and every task's evidence record in a way that cannot distinguish relevant from irrelevant edits.

Four largely independent 'immutable run/evidence directory' conventions have been built in parallel (Pipeline/TaskGraph/evidence, Pipeline/ArchitectureReview/outputs+evidence, Pipeline/Reconciliation/outputs/current+runs, Pipeline/AgentRuntime run artifacts) with subtly different atomicity/overwrite guarantees rather than one shared audit-artifact authority, increasing the surface where a future subsystem could get the immutability contract subtly wrong.

Execution authority is correctly centralized and fail-closed today (taskcontrol ready/authorize), but that discipline exists entirely in policy/tests, not in any mechanism preventing a future session from just implementing repository_write and wiring dispatch without an equivalent review gate — the 8/8 finding that stopped this before was itself a one-off human-triggered review, not a standing structural control.
gdd_iteration_concerns: No scoped impact analysis exists: any GDD edit invalidates all existing task conformance globally via a whole-file hash, regardless of relevance, which will not scale once more than one task has delivery evidence.

The only tool positioned to handle GDD change at scale (full Reconciliation + multi-model Verification Crew) is explicitly reserved for rare, expensive events, leaving no defined process for the common case of a small design tweak.

Task contracts embed gdd_evidence text snapshots at authoring time; there is no described mechanism for detecting when an evidence quote has silently drifted from current GDD wording short of the coarse whole-document hash check.
result.throughput_assessment: Zero measured throughput exists on the production path: the only delivered gameplay feature (NSC-023) predates and bypasses the current AgentRuntime/TaskExecution architecture, and two full days after Milestone 1 completed, all effort went into provider plumbing and self-review rather than gameplay work, despite the project's own ADR-019 principle to keep advancing the game. Until a write-capable worker actually lands one small merged gameplay change, 'days instead of weeks' is an unverified hypothesis, not a property of the current build.
human_intervention_points: Every task-scope/decomposition decision before handoff (explicitly required for NSC-003 before it may be worked).
Unity Play Mode verification and approval of delivery/baseline evidence records (human_approval.required gate).
PR review/merge — no automatic merge exists or is planned soon.
Revalidation approval after any GDD edit that flips existing evidence to needs_revalidation.
Exclusive-resource conflicts on shared Unity files (scenes, Input Actions, shared builders) since only one worker exists.
Artifact Authority Gate decisions whenever design is missing rather than merely unimplemented.

next_slice.title: Minimal write-capable single-task Implementer proof, isolated from the trusted-read repository root
next_slice.why: The architecture's single biggest untested claim is that a bounded worker can safely write scoped code and have that write independently verified. Nothing else in the roadmap (comparison pipelines, continuous autonomy, Progressive Decomposer) matters until this exists and is proven once on real Unity code.
deliverables: Add repository_write to ClaudeCodeProvider, invoked inside a disposable Git worktree/branch (never the trusted main checkout used for read-only ArchitectureReview), enabling Edit/Write only within request.write_boundaries.allowed_paths.

A deterministic post-invocation Git diff-scope check that rejects any commit touching a path outside allowed_paths before GER evaluation runs, reusing the already-implemented AgentInvocationRequest.is_path_writable.

Split the smallest possible sub-slice out of NSC-003 (e.g., the pure shared cursor-to-gameplay-plane projection function) per CURRENT_STATE's own note that NSC-003 should likely be decomposed before handoff, rather than handing over the full ticket.
Reuse the existing Assignment 6 GER pattern (static evaluator -> Unity Play Mode evidence -> refine -> circuit breaker) unchanged rather than inventing a new evaluation loop.
Keep dispatch manual and merge human-gated (no readiness/authorization changes).
next_slice.proof_of_value: One real, small, merged Unity code change produced end-to-end through AgentRuntime/TaskExecution with committed Phase 3A evidence proving conformant state — the first time the production path (not Assignment 5/6 ad hoc scripts) has ever shipped gameplay code.

do_not_build_yet: Provider fallback or a Claude-vs-Codex comparison/dual-provider launcher.
Continuous autonomy, dependency-derived readiness, or dispatch authorization.
Parallel workers or broad worktree orchestration.
Progressive Decomposer or Artifact Authority Gate as general platforms (build only if a specific near-frontier task actually hits a missing-design wall).
A scoped GDD impact-analysis engine — real, but defer until more than one task has delivery evidence to actually stress the whole-hash invalidation cost.

alternative_architecture.description: The state/authority primitives (immutable Git-anchored evidence, non-authoritative provider claims, mandatory runtime evidence, fail-closed capability contracts) do not need replacement. What's needed is resequencing: stop iterating on provider-adapter polish and self-review, and spend the next slice exclusively on the one missing capability (bounded repository_write plus worktree isolation) applied to a small real gameplay change.
alternative_architecture.why_better: A different architecture isn't indicated by the evidence gathered; the evidence shows a prioritization problem (meta-work over delivery), not a design-soundness problem. Rebuilding would discard genuinely sound, already-tested safety primitives to solve a sequencing issue.

evidence.observation: Confirms repository_write, approved_command_execution, dependency readiness, and dispatch authorization all remain unsupported/disabled as of the frozen commit, and that no real production revalidation record and no gameplay task execution have occurred since Milestone 1.
TaskExecutionRunner only publishes an audit record binding task identity to an AgentRuntime invocation; it explicitly excludes ExecutionCrew, Unity execution, GER, and Git operations.
_FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITIES rejects repository_write and approved_command_execution outright; only Read/Glob/Grep tools are ever enabled.
canon['sha256'] is compared against canonical_text_sha256 of the entire GDD file (CANON_PATH), so any GDD edit anywhere flips every task's evidence to needs_revalidation regardless of relevance.
CANON_PATH = 'Docs/GDD/No_Safe_Circle_GDD.md' confirms the hash is over the whole canonical document, not a task-scoped fragment.

Only ~10 gameplay scripts exist (door interaction, mana, WASD movement, camera follow) under a single DoorPrototype test area; NSC-003 mouse-directed movement, the designated real anchor task, has not been started.

repository_state_at_bootstrap: partial; current PlayerMovement.cs still only does WASD polling with no mouse-directed movement, confirming the flagship real-work anchor remains untouched by the pipeline.

Documents the real, concrete failures (camera facing wrong direction, no-op refinement) that motivated ADR-015/ADR-016 — evidence the architecture's core safety decisions trace to observed, not hypothetical, failure.

Synthesis prompt explicitly warns that reviewers 'share model-family biases and repeated claims are not independent proof,' showing deliberate awareness of correlated-LLM-failure risk in the review process itself, though no non-LLM or cross-family ground truth exists yet.
Explicitly accepts a trusted single-user read boundary instead of building a hardened sandbox, a proportionate and well-justified scope decision.

result.biggest_uncertainty: Whether, once repository_write is finally implemented, the existing contract/evidence/GER scaffolding will actually let a bounded worker deliver correct, mergeable Unity code fast enough to matter — this is completely untested in the current repository; every safety mechanism has been validated against a read-only meta-workload (reviewing the architecture itself), never against the real write-and-verify loop the whole system exists to enable.
